discovery: Rydberg-blockade interactions between individually controlled neutral atoms and their use for programmable quantum simulation and entanglement

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique / CNRS, Palaiseau, France

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austria

subfield: Atomic physics / quantum optics (quantum simulation with Rydberg atoms)
motivation: Zoller and Lukin, with co-workers, proposed in 2000-2001 that the strong dipolar interaction between Rydberg atoms blocks multiple excitation within micrometre distances, giving a controllable mechanism to entangle individual neutral atoms. Browaeys, with Grangier, observed the blockade and collective excitation between two single trapped atoms in 2009, then built reconfigurable optical-tweezer arrays of hundreds of atoms. Lukin's group developed defect-free arrays, observed quantum many-body scars, topological spin liquids and logical qubits with error correction. Together these works transformed Rydberg atoms, long a tool for cavity QED, into a programmable quantum matter platform where quantum magnetism, phase transitions and non-equilibrium dynamics are studied atom by atom with single-site readout. This is a striking example of patient control of single quanta yielding both fundamental insight into many-body quantum physics and a leading route to quantum computation.
